verdictLine: FIX FIRST (blocking F1): a path after `"` or `'`, the form in which Twig and the filter hand a plain string’s quotes to the engine, has its dashes and dots converted, against CHANGELOG.md:60; FU1–FU8 are not blocking (FU1 and FU2 are second-pass instabilities this range introduced under Fine typography and the styling hooks; FU7 is the release-day changelog heading and Hardened line).

findings.summary: A path after a quotation mark written as an entity is not recognised, so its dashes and dots are converted. Twig prints every `"` and `'` of a plain string as `"` and `'` (README.md:9), and the filter escapes a plain string the same way before the engine runs, so on the page pass and through `{{ value|sorts }}` the changelog’s “also after a quotation mark” does not hold: `Edit the file "/etc/my--app.conf" and restart.` printed from a plain-text field or a title gives `Edit the file “/etc/my—app.conf” and restart.`, while the same text from a rich-text field (raw `"`) gives `“/etc/my--app.conf”`. It reaches Lite (the filter) and Pro (the page pass) with the default rules. A URL is unaffected (`\b` before `https://` and `www.` matches after the `;`); only a path that starts with `/` is.

confirmedSound: The three guards bite: M1 (dashes), M2 (ellipsis) and M3 (typed-dashes) killed by the corpus; c483cc3’s fix bites as a whole (M4) and mark by mark (M5–M20, each of its 16 alternatives, killed by its own corpus case), and so do the straight quotes (M21), the /i flag (M23) and the inSpans search (M24, M27, M28).

The binary search is load-bearing for speed: the old linear walk (M30) fails exactly the two new guards at 15.3× and 14.4× after the retry, so the retry does not hide a quadratic pass. Every timing check in unit.php goes through `$retried`, and each call’s limit equals its check’s threshold (8, and 2 for the stray end tags); the retry measures both pages again and keeps the lower ratio, as 979b87b says (“at or over its limit”).

Every quotation mark any of the 16 locales writes (cs, da, de, de-CH, en-GB, en-US, es, fi, fr, fr-CH, it, nb, nl, pl, pt, sv, and the es guillemets-outer and de book variants) is in the guard’s list: a path in each locale’s curled quotes keeps its `--` and `...` on pass 1 and 2 (probe c3.txt). The marks written by the rules after priority 31 (primes, apostrophes, quotes, nbsp, locale spacing, widows) are all in the list.

With the default rules the guard is stable: in the gate’s sweep (3,000 generated inputs, 11 option sets: en-US, en-GB, fr, de, it, sv, text mode, the spaced-en-dash variant with typed-dashes, fr Bringhurst) every set but the English Bringhurst ones and the hooks has 0 unstable rows at HEAD, in line with the README’s sweep claim (README.md:369).

Attributes are never touched (`href`, `src`, `alt` keep `--` and `...`); `<code>`, `<pre>`, comments and `data-sorts="off"` are honoured; every example in README.md:374 and CHANGELOG.md:60 behaves as written; byte offsets hold after long multibyte and entity prefixes (corpus and probes).

At 900 KB (one URL word, one path word, 100,000 paths, 900 KB of slashes, 450,000 `"/` pairs, 60,000 curly-quoted paths) no PCRE error (`lastError()` null) and no pass over 0.42 s, default or Bringhurst.

bin/cldr-locales.mjs: its runtime block is byte-identical to mjs-tool-skeleton v0.5.0 (sha256 37931f3a… for both, 653 lines); a dry run against cldr-misc-full 49.0.0 reports all 16 locale files unchanged (“next: done  (dry run: nothing would change)”); help carries no escape byte when piped or under NO_COLOR or TERM=dumb, is bold on a terminal and under FORCE_COLOR=1, plain under FORCE_COLOR=0, and an empty NO_COLOR counts as unset, as its comment says; a missing or unknown command and an unknown option exit 2 with a usage hint, an unreadable package exits 3.

Scope: the range touches the files the brief names plus CHANGELOG.md, README.md, EFFORT.md (rows 28–30), gates/2026-11-07-sorts-d897-d898-recheck.json (49a181a) and comment-only ID-code renames in corpus 02, 05 and 15 (53510d1); none of those changes behaviour.
knownLimits: Marks glued to the end of a URL or path stay, as README.md:374 says: `(https://example.com/a--b)--then stop.`, `Visit https://example.com--it is great.`, `See https://example.com/a--b...` keep their `--` and `...`.

Not recognised, as README.md:374 lists: `example.com/a--b`, `ftp://example.com/a--b`, `mailto:a--b@example.com`, `a--b@example.com`, `//cdn.example.com/a--b.js`, `https://example.com/very-long--path`, `/a--b` are all converted.
A word of prose that starts with `/` is a path: `Use /s/ and /z/--the phonemes.` and `He said /no--wait/` keep `--` (README.md:374: a path is a word that starts with `/`).
CKEditor’s own autoformat turns `...` into `…` while typing, inside a URL too (README.md:256).

bin/cldr-locales.mjs (dev tooling, not read by the plugin): given the folder above the package, it says `cannot read <dir>/package.json` without saying the folder holding `main/` is wanted; Node’s own parseArgs message for an unknown option ends with an unbalanced quote (`as in '-- "--nope"`). Both predate the range.

notBlocking.summary:
Where ellipsis-spacing runs (the Bringhurst preset in English, or the rule switched on), it spaces a typed `…` inside a URL or a path. It runs at priority 21, after the ellipsis rule (20) has read the URL whole and before the dashes rule (30) reads it again, so (a) in one pass the URL’s `--` after the `…` is converted, against the new promise: `https://example.com/a…b/c--d` → `https://example.com/a … b/c – d`; and (b) the output is not stable: `

See https://example.com/a…b/c...d now

` → pass 1 `https://example.com/a … b/c...d`, pass 2 `https://example.com/a … b/c … d`. New in this range: the gate’s sweep has 0 unstable rows on 3edd0b1 and 258 + 258 of 6,000 in the en-US and en-GB Bringhurst sets at HEAD (on 3edd0b1 the URL’s dots were converted on pass 1). CKEditor turns a `...` typed in a URL into `…` (README.md:256), and a Pro page that prints `{{ field|sorts }}` is passed twice, since the page pass applies the engine to the whole page with only the skip tags (src/services/PagePass.php:76–77).

A URL or path is read to the next ASCII whitespace, not to the next space: a no-break space (U+00A0, U+202F, U+2009, ` `) does not end it, so prose joined to a path by one keeps its marks: `
